fullPassage:
Hi, everyone. My name is Minji Song, and I am the editor of an online teen magazine, Teens Today. I am honored to have been asked to give a talk. Many of our high school student subscribers send me messages with concerns about their future. So today, I will talk about the value of experiences in making a better future. For this talk, I asked my old friends to write down stories about what they experienced when they were younger. I would like to start by reading them one by one.

One summer day, I was watching an Olympic swimming event on TV. The gold medalist looked fantastic, and I wanted to be just like him. I asked my parents if I could learn to swim. They approved and said, "Yes." Swimming was difficult at first, but after a year, I became a good swimmer. I felt tired but happy when I was out of breath after every practice. As I practiced more, my times got better and better. One day, my coach suggested that I enter a competition. He also advised me that for good results I should build muscle strength through weight training. The training was demanding, leaving me exhausted at times. Whenever I felt this way, I told myself, "No pain, no gain."

I used to be quiet and shy when I was a child. My homeroom teacher told me one day that she was putting on a play for our school festival. She suggested that I take on a small role, saying that being in a play would be a good experience. So, I decided to do it. I was so nervous at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines at all. However, as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more confident. On the day of the performance, I got anxious and my mind went blank just before I stepped on the stage. My classmates tapped me on the shoulder and encouraged me. Thanks to this, I was able to perform my lines perfectly.

One day, I saw a poster advertising the city's landscape design contest. The instant I saw it, I got interested. After doing some research on the Internet, I discovered that landscape designing involves arranging and decorating outdoor spaces. I thought a landscape architect's work was impressive because the arrangement of plants and structures can transform a space. This inspired me to think about becoming a landscape architect. I found out that I had to be good at math and science in order to become a landscape architect. This is because landscape architects must calculate the dimensions and slopes of land as well as thoroughly examine environmental factors such as soil, air, and climate. I was not good at either subject at the time, so I decided to put more effort into studying them.

When I was fourteen, I was hospitalized for several weeks. One day, I saw a piece of paper on the table. I was bored, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time. I felt a sense of relief when I wrote what I wanted to do after leaving the hospital. That evening, I asked my mother to buy me a notebook. As I filled page after page, I realized that writing was more than just a way to kill time. As the years passed, my passion for writing grew stronger. So I started writing short stories and sharing them with my friends and family. I felt a sense of accomplishment whenever they told me my stories were good.

Can you guess what my friends do now? Are they a swimmer? An actor? A landscape architect? A novelist? Actually, all four of these people are me! I currently work as a magazine editor. As you can see, my preferences have changed over the years as I was exposed to new experiences. Every time my interest changed, I was worried about what I was going to become in the future. Do you also have similar concerns?

Changes in your interests and preferences are completely natural. Try to accept this process and keep an open mind. Exploring new things can sometimes lead to valuable experiences which will help shape your future. I myself tried many different things before I finally became an editor because I enjoyed writing. Thanks to these many interests, I can write articles about math and science, speak confidently in front of an audience, and relieve my stress by swimming.

Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a waste of time. Your school days are a time of self-discovery and personal growth. As you spend each day wisely, you will be able to figure out what kind of person you are and what you enjoy doing. Do not attempt to define yourself in just one way as you undergo this process. Be flexible. Remember that your potential is limitless.

When Steve Jobs was a college student, he did not know what he wanted to do in the future. He felt uncertain about how the normal classes he was required to take could help him figure out what to do with his life. He decided to start checking out things that seemed interesting to him. One day, he was walking around the college grounds and a poster caught his eye. The handwritten letters on every poster were elegant and beautiful. He became fascinated with the art of producing beautiful handwriting, also known as calligraphy, and decided to attend a calligraphy class. He gained an understanding of letter styles and learned to adjust the spacing between various combinations of letters. At that time, he did not expect that learning it would be useful or applicable to his life in the future. However, later when he developed his own computer operating system, he incorporated what he learned from that class into designing the system. As a result, he developed his own computer system with visually appealing letter styles. The artistic letters became a sensation at the time and are still widely used. His innovative incorporation of calligraphy into the world of technology, which started from his personal interest, has inspired many other corporations' computer system designs.

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I am honored to have been asked [to give / giving] a talk.

det.ref:
[원문] I am honored to have been asked to give a talk.
[해석] 저는 연설해 달라는 요청을 받아 영광입니다. [문장 04 참고]
det.correct: ask는 「ask + O + to-V」 구문을 취하는 동사이다. 수동태로 전환하면 「be asked to-V」가 되므로 to give가 정답.
wrongs: ① to give ✅ — ask + O + to-V의 수동태 be asked to-V에서 to부정사가 유지됨
② giving ❌ — ask는 동명사를 목적격보어로 취하지 않음
det.tip:
💡 핵심 문법: ask/tell/advise/want + O + to-V
• 수동태: be asked/told/advised/wanted + to-V
• to가 유지되는 것이 핵심

⚠️ 함정: suggest는 that절(should+V/V원형)을 취함 → to-V 불가

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 어휘를 고르시오.
For this talk, I asked my old friends to write down stories about what they [experienced / experiencing] when they were younger.

det.ref:
[원문] ...what they experienced when they were younger.
[해석] 그들이 더 어렸을 때 경험한 것에 대해 [문장 06 참고]
det.correct: what절 안에서 주어 they에 대한 동사가 필요하다. 과거 시제(when they were younger)와 일치하는 experienced가 정답.
wrongs: ① experienced ✅ — what절의 동사, 과거시제 일치
② experiencing ❌ — 동사 자리에 현재분사 단독 사용 불가
det.tip:
💡 관계대명사 what = the thing(s) which
• what + S + V: 주어+동사 필요

⚠️ 함정: what 뒤에 분사만 오면 동사 누락 오류

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I asked my parents [if / that] I could learn to swim.

det.ref:
[원문] I asked my parents if I could learn to swim.
[해석] 나는 부모님께 수영을 배울 수 있는지 여쭈었다. [문장 10 참고]
det.correct: ask가 "~인지 물어보다"의 의미일 때 if/whether절을 취한다. "~라고 말하다"가 아니므로 that은 부적절.
wrongs: ① if ✅ — ask + O + if절: ~인지 물어보다
② that ❌ — ask + that은 "요청하다" 의미에서 that S (should) V 구문이나, 여기서는 의문의 의미
det.tip:
💡 ask의 두 가지 용법
• ask + O + if/whether: ~인지 물어보다
• ask + that + S + (should) V: ~을 요청하다

⚠️ 문맥에 따라 구분!

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I felt tired but happy when I was out of breath after every practice. As I practiced more, my times got [better and better / more better].

det.ref:
[원문] As I practiced more, my times got better and better.
[해석] 연습할수록 나의 기록은 점점 더 좋아졌다. [문장 13 참고]
det.correct: 비교급 강조는 「비교급 + and + 비교급」 패턴을 사용한다. better는 이미 비교급이므로 more를 붙이면 이중 비교급 오류.
wrongs: ① better and better ✅ — 비교급+and+비교급: 점점 더
② more better ❌ — better 자체가 비교급이므로 more 중복 불가
det.tip:
💡 비교급 and 비교급 = 점점 더 ~
• 1음절: taller and taller
• 2음절 이상: more and more beautiful
• 불규칙: better and better / worse and worse

⚠️ more better, most best 등 이중비교 절대 금지

questions.passage: One day, my coach suggested that I enter a competition. He also advised me that for good results I should build muscle strength through weight training. The training was demanding, leaving me exhausted at times. ( ___ ) I felt this way, I told myself, "No pain, no gain."
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 연결사를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 8자, W로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] Whenever I felt this way, I told myself, "No pain, no gain."
[해석] 이런 식으로 느낄 때마다 나는 스스로에게 말했다. [문장 17 참고]
det.correct: 문맥상 "~할 때마다"의 의미를 가진 접속사가 필요하다. Whenever = every time (that).
det.tip:
💡 시간 부사절 접속사
• whenever = every time that (~할 때마다)
• while = during the time that (~하는 동안)

⚠️ every time과 whenever는 교환 가능하지만, every time 뒤에 that 생략 가능

questions.passage: I used to be quiet and shy when I was a child. My homeroom teacher told me one day that she was putting on a play for our school festival. She suggested that I take on a small role, saying that being in a play would be a good experience. So, I decided to do <u>it</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 it이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] She suggested that I take on a small role...So, I decided to do it.
[해석] 선생님이 작은 역할을 맡으라고 제안했고, 그래서 나는 그것을 하기로 결정했다. [문장 19~21 참고]
det.correct: it은 바로 앞 문장에서 선생님이 제안한 "take on a small role(작은 역할을 맡는 것)"을 가리킨다.
wrongs: ① ❌ — 축제 준비가 아닌 역할 맡기를 제안받음
② ✅ — take on a small role을 지칭
③ ❌ — 축제 참가가 아닌 연극 출연
④ ❌ — 문맥과 무관
⑤ ❌ — 선생님 돕기는 언급 없음
det.tip:
💡 대명사 it의 지칭 추론
• 바로 앞 문장에서 언급된 행위/사물을 우선 확인
• suggest/advise 뒤 that절 내용이 it의 대상인 경우 빈출

⚠️ it이 가리키는 범위를 너무 넓게 잡지 말 것

ch: ② 연극에서 작은 역할을 맡는 것

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I was so nervous at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines [at all / at once].

det.ref:
[원문] I was so nervous at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines at all.
[해석] 첫 리허설에서 너무 긴장해서 대사를 전혀 말할 수 없었다. [문장 22 참고]
det.correct: 부정문에서 "전혀 ~않다"는 not ~ at all이다. at once는 "즉시, 동시에"의 의미로 문맥에 부적절.
wrongs: ① at all ✅ — not ~ at all: 전혀 ~않다
② at once ❌ — "즉시" 또는 "동시에"라는 의미로 문맥 부적절
det.tip:
💡 at 관련 숙어
• not ~ at all: 전혀 ~않다
• at once: 즉시 / 동시에
• at times: 때때로
• at first: 처음에

⚠️ so ~ that 구문: so + 형/부 + that + S + V

questions.passage: However, as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more ( ___ ).
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 9자, c로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] ...as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more confident.
[해석] 대사를 더 연습할수록 점점 더 자신감이 생겼다. [문장 23 참고]
det.correct: 비교급+and+비교급 패턴에서 more and more confident가 원문이다. confident(자신감 있는)가 정답.
det.tip:
💡 비교급+and+비교급 with 다음절 형용사
• more and more + 형용사: 점점 더 ~한
• confident ↔ nervous (반의어)

⚠️ confidence(명사)와 confident(형용사) 구분!

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 가장 적절한 표현을 고르시오.
On the day of the performance, I got anxious and my mind went [blank / black] just before I stepped on the stage.

det.ref:
[원문] ...my mind went blank just before I stepped on the stage.
[해석] 무대에 오르기 직전에 불안해져서 머릿속이 하얗게 되었다. [문장 24 참고]
det.correct: go blank는 "머릿속이 하얗게 되다, 아무 생각이 나지 않다"라는 관용 표현이다.
wrongs: ① blank ✅ — go blank: 머릿속이 하얗게 되다
② black ❌ — go black은 "시야가 검게 변하다"(기절)의 의미로 문맥 부적절
det.tip:
💡 go + 형용사 관용 표현
• go blank: 머릿속이 하얗게 되다
• go wrong: 잘못되다
• go bad: 상하다

⚠️ go + 형용사는 주로 부정적 변화를 나타냄

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
My classmates tapped me on the shoulder and [encouraged / encouraging] me.

det.ref:
[원문] My classmates tapped me on the shoulder and encouraged me.
[해석] 반 친구들이 내 어깨를 두드리며 격려해 주었다. [문장 26 참고]
det.correct: and는 등위접속사로 tapped와 encouraged를 병렬 연결한다. 같은 시제(과거형)로 맞추어야 함.
wrongs: ① encouraged ✅ — tapped and encouraged: 과거형 병렬
② encouraging ❌ — tapped(과거)와 병렬이 안 됨
det.tip:
💡 등위접속사 and의 병렬 구조
• A and B → 같은 품사/형태
• tapped and encouraged (과거+과거) ✅
• tapped and encouraging (과거+현재분사) ❌

⚠️ 병렬 구조는 내신 최빈출 어법 포인트!

questions.stem:
다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 고르시오.
One day, I saw a poster ⓐadvertising the city's landscape design contest. The instant I saw it, I got interested. After ⓑdoing some research on the Internet, I discovered that landscape designing ⓒinvolve arranging and decorating outdoor spaces. I thought a landscape architect's work was impressive ⓓbecause the arrangement of plants and structures can transform a space. This inspired me ⓔto think about becoming a landscape architect.

det.ref:
[원문] ...I discovered that landscape designing involves arranging...
[해석] 조경 디자인이 야외 공간을 배치하고 장식하는 것을 포함한다는 것을 알게 되었다. [문장 30 참고]
det.correct: 주어 landscape designing은 동명사구로 단수 취급. 따라서 동사는 involves(3인칭 단수)가 되어야 한다. involve → involves.
wrongs: ⓐ advertising ✅ — 현재분사: a poster를 수식 (광고하는 포스터)
ⓑ doing ✅ — 전치사 after 뒤 동명사 적절
ⓒ involve ❌ → involves — 동명사 주어는 단수 취급
ⓓ because ✅ — 이유를 나타내는 접속사로 적절
ⓔ to think ✅ — inspire + O + to-V 구문 적절
det.tip:
💡 동명사(구) 주어의 수일치
• Studying math is important. (단수)
• Swimming and running are good. (복수)

⚠️ designing이 주어 → involves (단수동사)

questions.passage: I found out that I had to be good at math and science in order to become a landscape architect. This is because landscape architects must calculate the ( ___ ) and slopes of land.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 10자, d로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] ...landscape architects must calculate the dimensions and slopes of land...
[해석] 조경 건축가는 토지의 치수와 경사를 계산해야 한다. [문장 33 참고]
det.correct: dimension(치수, 규모)의 복수형 dimensions가 정답. 토지의 dimensions and slopes를 계산한다는 문맥.
det.tip:
💡 dimension (n.) 치수, 규모, 차원
• calculate the dimensions: 치수를 계산하다
• 복수형으로 주로 사용됨

⚠️ dimension vs. direction 혼동 주의

questions.passage: This is because landscape architects must calculate the dimensions and slopes of land ( ___ ) thoroughly examine environmental factors such as soil, air, and climate.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 표현을 쓰시오. (3단어 → 객관식으로 전환)

det.ref:
[원문] ...as well as thoroughly examine environmental factors...
[해석] 환경 요인을 철저히 조사할 뿐만 아니라 [문장 34 참고]
det.correct: A as well as B: A뿐만 아니라 B도. calculate와 examine을 연결하는 표현.
det.tip:
💡 as well as = in addition to
• A as well as B → A뿐만 아니라 B도
• 수일치: as well as 앞의 주어에 맞춤

⚠️ not only A but also B와 비교!

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I was not good at [either / neither] subject at the time, so I decided to put more effort into studying them.

det.ref:
[원문] I was not good at either subject at the time...
[해석] 나는 그때 두 과목 모두에 능하지 못했다. [문장 35 참고]
det.correct: not ~ either는 "둘 다 ~않다"의 의미. neither는 그 자체로 부정이므로 not과 함께 쓰면 이중부정.
wrongs: ① either ✅ — not ~ either: 둘 다 ~않다
② neither ❌ — not + neither는 이중부정 오류
det.tip:
💡 either vs. neither
• not ~ either = neither: 둘 다 ~않다
• either: 긍정문/의문문/부정문에서 사용
• neither: 그 자체가 부정 → not과 함께 불가

⚠️ 이중부정 함정 빈출!

questions.stem:
다음 한국어를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
"나는 지루해서 그것을 집어 들고 시간을 보내기 위해 무언가를 쓰기 시작했다."

det.ref:
[원문] I was bored, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time.
[해석] 나는 지루해서 그것을 집어 들고 시간을 보내기 위해 무언가를 쓰기 시작했다. [문장 37 참고]
det.correct: bored(지루해하는)가 사람의 감정 상태를 나타냄. pick it up(대명사는 사이에), begin + V-ing, to pass(목적의 to부정사) 모두 적절.
wrongs: ① ❌ — boring은 "지루하게 하는"으로 사물 수식
② ✅ — bored, pick it up, began writing, to pass 모두 정확
③ ❌ — picked up it(X) → picked it up(O), for passing(X) → to pass(O)
④ ❌ — Being boring: 주어가 사람이므로 Being bored가 올바름
⑤ ❌ — began to writing(X) → began writing 또는 began to write
det.tip:
💡 감정 형용사 -ed vs. -ing
• -ed: 감정을 느끼는 사람 (bored, excited)
• -ing: 감정을 유발하는 대상 (boring, exciting)

⚠️ 대명사 + 타동사구: pick it up (O) / pick up it (X)

ch: ① I was boring, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time.
② I was bored, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time.
③ I was bored, so I picked up it and began to write things down for passing the time.
④ Being boring, I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time.
⑤ I was bored, so I picked it up and began to writing things down to pass the time.

questions.passage: As I filled page after page, I realized that writing was more than just a way to <u>kill time</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 kill time과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] ...writing was more than just a way to kill time.
[해석] 글쓰기는 단지 시간을 때우는 방법 이상이라는 것을 깨달았다. [문장 41 참고]
det.correct: kill time = "시간을 때우다, 목적 없이 시간을 보내다". pass time without purpose가 가장 가까운 의미.
wrongs: ① ❌ — waste hours는 "시간을 낭비하다"로 부정적 뉘앙스가 더 강함
② ❌ — productively(생산적으로)는 kill time의 반대 의미
③ ✅ — kill time ≈ pass time without purpose
det.tip:
💡 kill time = 시간을 때우다
• 목적 없이 시간을 보내는 것
• pass the time과 유사하지만 좀 더 informal

⚠️ kill time ≠ waste time (낭비)

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I felt a sense of accomplishment [whenever / however] they told me my stories were good.

det.ref:
[원문] I felt a sense of accomplishment whenever they told me my stories were good.
[해석] 그들이 내 이야기가 좋다고 말할 때마다 성취감을 느꼈다. [문장 44 참고]
det.correct: 문맥상 "~할 때마다"의 의미가 필요. whenever = every time that.
wrongs: ① whenever ✅ — ~할 때마다
② however ❌ — "그러나" 또는 "아무리 ~해도"로 문맥 부적절
det.tip:
💡 whenever vs. however
• whenever: ~할 때마다
• however: 그러나 / 아무리 ~해도

⚠️ however + 형/부 + S + V: 양보 (아무리 ~해도)

questions.stem:
주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열한 것을 고르시오.
As you can see, my preferences (changed / over / have / the years) as I was exposed to new experiences.

det.ref:
[원문] ...my preferences have changed over the years...
[해석] 세월이 흐르면서 나의 취향이 변해왔다. [문장 47 참고]
det.correct: 현재완료(have changed) + 기간 부사구(over the years)의 어순. have+p.p. 사이에 부사구가 끼어들지 않는 것이 자연스럽다.
wrongs: ① ✅ — have changed over the years: 자연스러운 어순
② ❌ — changed have: 어순 오류
③ ❌ — 부사구가 동사 앞: 비문법적
④ ❌ — have와 changed 사이에 부사구 삽입: 어색
⑤ ❌ — the years over: 전치사구 어순 오류
det.tip:
💡 현재완료 + 기간 부사
• have + p.p. + over the years/for years
• over the years: 세월에 걸쳐

⚠️ 현재완료는 과거~현재의 계속/경험/완료/결과

ch: ① have changed over the years
② changed have over the years
③ over the years have changed
④ have over the years changed
⑤ the years over have changed

questions.passage: Every time my interest changed, I was worried about what I was going to become in the future. Do you also have similar concerns? Changes in your interests and preferences are completely natural. Try to accept <u>this process</u> and keep an open mind.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 this process가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] Changes in your interests and preferences are completely natural. Try to accept this process...
[해석] 관심사와 취향의 변화는 완전히 자연스럽다. 이 과정을 받아들여라. [문장 49~50 참고]
det.correct: this process는 바로 앞 문장의 "Changes in your interests and preferences(관심사와 취향의 변화)"를 가리킨다.
wrongs: ① ❌ — 직업 결정이 아닌 관심사 변화를 의미
② ✅ — 관심사와 취향이 변화하는 과정
③ ❌ — 워크북은 본문과 무관
④ ❌ — 거부가 아닌 변화 자체
⑤ ❌ — 글쓰기만이 아닌 전반적 관심사 변화
det.tip:
💡 this/these + 명사의 지칭
• 바로 앞 문장(들)의 핵심 내용을 지칭하는 경우가 대부분

⚠️ this가 가리키는 범위: 직전 문장 우선 확인

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
Exploring new things can sometimes lead to valuable experiences [which / what] will help shape your future.

det.ref:
[원문] Exploring new things can sometimes lead to valuable experiences which will help shape your future.
[해석] 새로운 것을 탐구하면 미래를 형성하는 데 도움이 될 귀중한 경험을 얻을 수 있다. [문장 51 참고]
det.correct: 선행사 valuable experiences가 있으므로 관계대명사 which가 적절. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 불가.
wrongs: ① which ✅ — 선행사 experiences + 주격 관계대명사
② what ❌ — what = the thing(s) which: 선행사 포함이므로 선행사가 있을 때 불가
det.tip:
💡 which vs. what (관계대명사)
• which: 선행사 있을 때 → experiences which...
• what: 선행사 없을 때 → what I learned...

⚠️ which/what 구분은 "선행사 유무"로 판단!

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
[Allowing / Allowed] yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a waste of time.

det.ref:
[원문] Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a waste of time.
[해석] 다양한 것을 경험할 기회를 스스로에게 허락하는 것은 시간 낭비가 아니다. [문장 55 참고]
det.correct: 문장의 주어 자리에 동명사(V-ing)가 오고 is로 연결된다. Allowing ~ things가 주어부, is가 동사.
wrongs: ① Allowing ✅ — 동명사 주어: Allowing ~ is not...
② Allowed ❌ — 과거분사는 주어 역할 불가 (수동의미 부적절)
det.tip:
💡 동명사 주어
• V-ing + ... + is/was: 동명사구 주어 = 단수 취급
• Allowing yourself ~ is not a waste.

⚠️ 동명사 vs. 현재분사 구분: 문장에서 역할(주어/보어/목적어)로 판단

questions.passage: As you spend each day wisely, you will be able to ( ___ ) out what kind of person you are and what you enjoy doing.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 6자, f로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] ...you will be able to figure out what kind of person you are...

det.correct: figure out = ~을 알아내다, 이해하다. 문맥상 자아를 발견하는 과정.
det.tip:
💡 figure out = 알아내다, 파악하다
• figure out + 명사/의문사절
• find out과 유사한 의미

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
He felt uncertain about how the normal classes he was required [to take / taking] could help him figure out what to do with his life.

det.ref:

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.

wrongs: ① producing ✅ — 전치사 of + 동명사: the art of producing

💡 전치사 + 동명사(V-ing)

• 전치사 뒤에는 반드시 명사/동명사
